draft.title: Supply
card: Supply is how much of a product sellers will offer for sale at each price.
As the price rises, sellers usually offer more. A higher price means more money for each item sold.
As the price falls, sellers usually offer less. Some items may no longer be worth making at a low price.
Supply describes the sellers' side of a market. It is a different idea from demand.

2.alt: A supply curve sloping up. When the price rises from a low price to a high price, sellers offer more: the quantity offered rises from fewer to more, from A to B along the curve.

draft.remember: Higher price, sellers usually offer more. Lower price, they usually offer less.

a.q: Which of these best describes what supply means in a market?
opts: How much sellers will offer at each price
How much buyers want to buy at each price
How much a product costs to make
How many sellers there are in a market
a.why: Supply is the amount sellers will offer at each price. The option about buyers is not supply, because supply describes the sellers' side of a market.
a.clue: Supply is about the sellers' side of the market.

b.q: At a Yarra Valley farm stand, the price of strawberries rises from $4 to $6 a punnet. What will the farm usually do?
opts: Offer the same number of punnets
Stop selling punnets at the gate
b.why: A higher price means more money for each punnet, so the Yarra Valley farm usually offers more. Offering fewer would match a price fall, not a rise.
b.clue: What does a higher price mean for the seller's income?

a.best: How much sellers will offer at each price
